program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-entry deep passes; consolidate and validate once after Wave 2500

source_provenance: Public PubMed/PMC abstracts and ordinary web research
manual clinical-identity, route, formulation, population, observational, implementation, evidence-quality and safety calibration

policy.validation_strategy: deep source calibration per pass; expensive repository-wide validation after Wave 2500

rejected_candidates.title: Reproductive risks and fertility preservation in women treated with radioactive iodine therapy for thyroid cancer.
rejected_candidates.reason: radioactive iodine cancer therapy is not nutritional iodine or supplement evidence

rejected_candidates.title: Development and Validation of Questionnaires for Quantifying Intake from Dietary Supplements: A Scoping Review.
rejected_candidates.reason: dietary-assessment methodology rather than supplement efficacy, safety, interaction, or clinically actionable evidence

waves.title: Improving Cognition in Bipolar Disorder: A Systematic Review of Current Pharmacological and Nutraceutical Approaches.
waves.study: systematic review with narrative synthesis of 16 studies/13 agents
waves.population: adults aged 18-65 with euthymic or partially remitted bipolar disorder
waves.finding: Among nutraceutical-relevant agents, ashwagandha showed cognitive benefit in a single study while DHA showed no significant effect; the wider review found inconsistent cognitive outcomes across agents and study quality ranged from good to poor.
waves.safety: Single-study nutraceutical signals are insufficient for an ingredient-level cognitive recommendation in bipolar disorder.

waves.title: Effect of curcumin on inflammatory markers and disease activity in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: A meta-analysis.
waves.finding: Curcumin significantly reduced DAS-28, rheumatoid factor, ESR, and CRP in pooled analyses, but heterogeneity was substantial and longer exposure-verified trials are needed.
waves.safety: Adjunctive RA evidence is condition-specific and does not establish long-term disease modification or a universal formulation/dose.

waves.title: Oral or parenteral iron supplementation to reduce deferral, iron deficiency and/or anaemia in blood donors.
waves.finding: Oral iron probably reduced low-hemoglobin donation deferral and may improve hemoglobin and ferritin; gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent. IV iron increased hemoglobin and ferritin but evidence for several outcomes remained uncertain.
waves.safety: Benefit and gastrointestinal harm should be preserved together; donor-specific supplementation should be targeted by iron status rather than generalized to healthy non-donors.

waves.title: Selenium supplementation and male fertility: Mechanistic insights and therapeutic potential.
waves.study: narrative/mechanistic review with human and animal evidence
waves.finding: The review describes selenium-dependent antioxidant mechanisms and limited human signals for sperm motility/fertility, while emphasizing a U-shaped exposure relationship in which excessive intake can impair sperm motility.
waves.safety: Mixed animal/human evidence and selenium's narrow safety margin prevent dose inference; toxicity risk is central to interpretation.

waves.title: Vitamin D status, supplementation, and multiple sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis of status studies plus 22 supplementation studies
waves.population: people with multiple sclerosis and healthy controls
waves.finding: MS was associated with lower vitamin-D status, but overall supplementation did not significantly reduce annualized relapse rate or improve disability; high-dose subgroup signals suggested lower relapse risk without clear disability benefit.
waves.safety: Status association, overall randomized effect, and high-dose subgroup findings must remain separate; subgroup signals do not justify unsupervised high-dose dosing.

waves.title: Effectiveness of mHealth-Based Nutritional Interventions on Iron Status of Pregnant Women: Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
waves.population: pregnant women receiving mobile-health-supported nutritional interventions
waves.finding: Nine of 11 trials reported improved hemoglobin with mHealth-supported nutrition/supplement interventions, with some clinically large changes, but delivery modes and intervention components were too heterogeneous for meta-analysis.
waves.safety: This evaluates implementation/adherence strategies rather than isolating iron-supplement efficacy.

waves.title: Xanthohumol: Mechanistic Actions and Emerging Evidence as a Multi-Target Natural Nutraceutical.
waves.population: predominantly preclinical evidence with small human safety/pharmacology studies
waves.finding: Xanthohumol modulates multiple inflammatory, redox, metabolic, and cell-signaling pathways; human studies mainly support tolerability and biomarker effects rather than established disease efficacy.
waves.safety: Clinical relevance remains unproven for most disease claims; bioavailability/formulation is a major translational limitation.

waves.title: High-dose vitamin C supplementation in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: A pilot randomized, triple-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
waves.population: 31 adults undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation
waves.finding: High-dose IV then oral vitamin C corrected plasma vitamin-C levels, while trends toward less graft-versus-host disease and oral mucositis were not statistically significant.
waves.safety: Very small pilot, mixed IV/oral route, high-risk transplant population, and non-significant clinical outcomes preclude efficacy promotion.

waves.title: Effectiveness of Korean Red Ginseng on fatigue in patients with rheumatic diseases: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.
waves.population: 120 patients with Sjogren syndrome and/or rheumatoid arthritis
waves.finding: Korean Red Ginseng did not significantly outperform placebo for fatigue improvement at 12 weeks; both groups improved.
waves.safety: Pruritus and urticaria were among the most frequent adverse events; results are specific to Korean Red Ginseng and rheumatic-disease fatigue.

waves.title: Efficacy of melatonin on drug- or contrast-induced acute kidney injury: a systematic review and GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of experimental and clinical studies.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis of 29 animal studies and 5 clinical trials
waves.population: experimental AKI models and human clinical studies
waves.finding: Melatonin improved drug-induced AKI markers in animal models but did not significantly reduce creatinine, BUN, or AKI incidence in clinical studies; clinical certainty was very low.
waves.safety: Human null evidence must take precedence over positive animal signals when discussing clinical efficacy.

waves.title: Dual impact of Ashwagandha: Significant cortisol reduction but no effects on perceived stress - A systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.finding: Ashwagandha significantly reduced cortisol but did not significantly improve perceived-stress scores in pooled analysis.
waves.safety: Biomarker improvement and subjective clinical benefit diverged; cortisol reduction should not be presented as proof of stress relief.

waves.title: Effect of early-life protein supplementation on childhood obesity and related metabolic outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: children exposed to differing protein quantity/source during complementary feeding
waves.finding: Higher-protein interventions did not substantially change weight-for-length, fat-free mass, or fat mass in pooled analyses.
waves.safety: This is early-life feeding evidence, not evidence for protein powders or adult supplementation.

waves.title: Baseline omega-3 nutritional status and supplementation response in pediatric attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review and biomarker-stratified meta-analysis.
waves.finding: Omega-3 produced a small overall symptom benefit; estimated effects were larger in children with low baseline omega-3 biomarkers and absent in normal/high or unstratified groups.
waves.safety: Only seven RCTs contributed and baseline-deficiency definitions differed; biomarker-guided supplementation remains hypothesis-generating.

waves.title: A systematic review and dose response meta analysis of Omega 3 supplementation on cognitive function.
waves.finding: Omega-3 supplementation was associated with modest improvements across several cognitive domains, with low-to-moderate certainty and nonlinear dose-response patterns for some outcomes.
waves.safety: Nonlinear meta-regression cannot define an optimal dose; long-term confirmatory trials are needed.

waves.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Exercise, Protein Supplementation, and Combined Interventions for Sarcopenia Management in Women: A Network Meta-Analysis.
waves.finding: Exercise plus nutritional supplementation ranked best for several strength/function outcomes, while nutritional supplementation alone did not significantly improve any assessed outcome.
waves.safety: Combined-intervention benefit cannot be assigned to protein supplementation alone.

waves.title: Exploring vitamin D levels and the impact of vitamin D supplementation in pregnant women with diabetes: meta-analysis.
waves.study: meta-analysis of observational and intervention studies
waves.finding: Women with GDM had lower vitamin-D status, and supplementation reliably raised 25(OH)D; evidence for downstream metabolic benefit was less clearly established than correction of deficiency.
waves.safety: Pregnancy and diabetes are special clinical contexts, and dose/timing regimens varied widely.

waves.title: Probiotic, Prebiotic, or Synbiotic Supplementation in Parkinson's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis with Trial Sequential Analysis.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis
waves.finding: Microbiome-targeting supplements improved constipation-related outcomes; motor-symptom improvement was uncertain and evidence certainty was very low.
waves.safety: Interventions pooled different probiotic, prebiotic, and synbiotic products, so category-wide neurologic efficacy is unsupported.

waves.title: Efficacy and Safety of Steamed Ginger Extract for Body Weight and Body Fat Reduction in Overweight Adults: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial.
waves.finding: A proprietary GD-standardized steamed ginger extract reduced body-fat percentage/mass, weight, BMI, waist and hip circumference, triglycerides, and total cholesterol versus placebo.
waves.safety: No product-related adverse events were reported, but findings are specific to one standardized proprietary extract and a small trial.

waves.title: Comparison of the Effect of Hypericum perforatum Vaginal Gel and Clotrimazole Vaginal Cream on Vaginal Candida albicans Infection: A Double-Blind Randomized Clinical Trial.
waves.population: 80 women with microbiologically confirmed vulvovaginal candidiasis
waves.finding: Both intravaginal Hypericum gel and clotrimazole improved symptoms; Hypericum was not superior overall, with symptom-domain differences between groups.
waves.safety: This is intravaginal topical therapy and cannot support oral St John's wort efficacy; no adverse events were reported.

waves.title: Effects of curcumin and Curcuma longa extract on inflammatory biomarkers in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE): a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.finding: Curcumin/Curcuma did not significantly improve DAS-28, ESR, or CRP, with very high heterogeneity across all outcomes.
waves.safety: Useful direct null/mixed evidence; inflammatory-marker claims should not be inferred from smaller individual trials when pooled evidence is null.

waves.title: Iodine supplementation for preventing iodine deficiency disorders in children and adolescents.
waves.finding: Iodine supplementation slightly improved cognition, likely reduced hypothyroidism, and reduced infant mortality in one study; growth changed little and evidence for goiter was very uncertain.
waves.safety: Adverse events were not reported; applicability depends on iodine-deficiency risk and several studies used large single doses rather than routine daily supplementation.

waves.title: Effects of Omega-3 Fatty Acid Treatment on Risk for Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Meta-Analysis of 35 Trials including 114 592 Individuals.
waves.population: 114,592 adults, generally age 50+ across cardiovascular-risk strata
waves.finding: High-dose EPA/DHA above 1,500 mg/day increased new-onset atrial-fibrillation risk in people at high cardiovascular risk (OR 1.43; absolute risk difference about 0.8%); lower-dose regimens did not show a significant AF increase.
waves.safety: Important dose-and-risk-context safety signal; benefit-risk assessment should preserve both cardiovascular indication and arrhythmia risk rather than imply a universal cutoff.

waves.title: Association Between Dietary/Supplementary Calcium Intake and Risk of Breast Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Cohort Studies.
waves.finding: Higher total calcium intake was associated with modestly lower breast-cancer risk, but supplemental calcium alone was not significantly associated with lower risk.
waves.safety: Observational dietary associations do not establish calcium-supplement cancer prevention.

waves.title: Exploratory pilot trial of astaxanthin supplementation in PCOS patients at risk of OHSS with focus on RAGE-NFκB pathway.
waves.population: 44 women with PCOS at high risk for ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome
waves.finding: Astaxanthin increased oocyte maturity and favorably shifted inflammatory RAGE-NFκB-related biomarkers, but the pilot was not powered to confirm the primary OHSS endpoint.
waves.safety: Exploratory assisted-reproduction population; surrogate/mechanistic changes do not establish prevention of OHSS.

waves.title: Efficacy of melatonin as adjunctive therapy for sepsis: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.finding: Adjunctive melatonin was associated with lower mortality in pooled trials (OR 0.42), alongside anti-inflammatory signals.
waves.safety: Small total sample in a high-acuity clinical setting; this is not general supplement-use evidence and requires larger high-quality trials before practice-level inference.
